title: Opposite-direction positions on the same symbol (any accounts, any strategies) raise a review alert; the review decides keep both / close one side, from evidence
note: Operator 2026-11-11 ~22:30Z, verbatim: 'right now we're holding on the prop accounts 2 soul positions that are short and 1 that's long ... it should, like, raise at least a red flag for review ... if the system now thinks that soul is going to go up, then we should probably get out of the short trades, especially since they're currently profitable ... I'm not saying that we should have a rule against it ... but we should understand what circumstances justify doing that, and if it's not the situation, then it should be like an alert that we probably need to close one side of that trade.' Instance: SOL short on velotrade_1 and tradeify_1 (trend_donchian_sol_4h) vs SOL long on breakout_2 (prop-manual-de7e925668af, entry 84.81, SL 83.11, TP 87.36). Deliverables: (1) an immediate review of the SOL book; (2) a detector: any symbol with net-opposing open positions across the books raises ONE alert and dispatches a live review (alert, not a gate, never auto-closes); (3) a pre-registered research unit: when do opposite-direction legs on one symbol both keep positive expectancy (timeframe separation, regime), measured from backtest overlap, so the review has a rule of thumb. FINDING 2026-11-15 (manager ask, AM-OPS measured): the ETHUSDT conflict re-alerted 3 times tonight. Each time it fired a high alert, a Telegram message and a paid review, and both reviews returned the same HOLD. The key is NOT hashing anything that churns: conflict_key() is already sha1(sorted long ids; sorted short ids), the shape the manager proposed. I reproduced all three keys exactly from package ids. Long side is always [pkg-ec790aada2a548dc ml_entry_v2]. Short side: f9b0dbe1d5 (00:10Z) = {48c5cfab eth_4h, 665b2dff eth_4h, edd087a2 trend_donchian_eth, fd522972 trend_donchian_eth_prop}. 43d62acadb (02:20Z) is the same minus fd522972, whose package closed 02:20:38Z. 71bffc9581 (03:01Z) is the same minus edd087a2, closed 03:01:58Z. So every re-fire was one short leg EXITING; the conflict only shrank, while the opposing core (ml_entry_v2 long vs eth_4h short) stayed constant. XRP is the same mechanism: long pkg-d7cb5eff ml_entry_v2 vs shorts {a7b186d4 xrp_4h, ea232fa1 xrp_adx25}. a7b186d4 closed 03:03:15Z, so expect one more XRP re-alert at about 03:03Z. PROPOSAL (no new gate): re-alert and queue a review only when a package NOT in the already-alerted set for that symbol JOINS the conflict. A leg leaving (live set a subset of the alerted set, both sides still non-empty) carries the record forward under the new key with no send and no review event. Resolution (one side empties) still clears the record, so a recurrence alerts as now. Code: alert() in src/runtime/conflicting_exposure.py (match a live key to a stored record of the same symbol whose packages are a superset) and the conflicting_exposure level in live_review_due.py (that path uses the review index, so it needs the same subset carry-forward, e.g. level = the key of the first-alerted superset record). Tier 2 (alert and review-wake path, not the order path). Owner AM-TRADING; AM-OPS can build it if the manager routes it. Fix built (manager decision 03:08Z): PR #26190 (0edf7d9f), Tier 2 hold, restart batch. carry_forward() keeps the alerted key while the live set is a subset of the alerted set. Applied in detect() (review level) and alert(). Tests pin tonight's 3 ETH keys giving 1 alert; joiners still alert. Observation to close the row: the next shrink-only conflict shows 'standing', not 'sent', in the wake-post record and queues no new review. #26190 MERGED 03:47Z at head 0edf7d9f (squash 268b4fed); deploy by git-sync restart pending. landed_unproven. CLOSING OBSERVATION: the next leg EXIT from a standing ETH or XRP conflict produces NO new conflicting_exposure alert (wake-post record shows 'standing', not 'sent') and NO new LTR conflicting_exposure wake for its packages, while a genuinely new joiner still alerts. Also confirm the restart's boot_audit shows every position accounted for with SL+TP intact. DEPLOYED: the trader restarted onto 268b4fe (#26190 +6) at 03:49:41Z. boot_audit: all live trades accounted for, 16/16 broker positions tracked, SL+TP at broker 16/16, 11 live accounts (3 prop not broker-readable). Exit-eval restart gap 17.8 s. Merged + deployed; NOT yet observed (waiting for a leg exit from the standing ETH/XRP conflict). 16:30Z #26190 OBSERVED: the claude_desk SOL short (pkg-00ba211201bd4..., bybit_1) left the standing SOL conflict (alerted 08:12:08Z / 10:06:51Z) on its SL at 13:21:48Z and NO conflict re-alert followed (next/last conflict alert 12:00:59Z BTC, read of /api/bot/alerts since 08:00Z). Each conflict alert after the 03:48Z merge was a NEW leg entering (08:12 desk short, 09:19 ict_scalp_eth_15m, 10:06 ict_scalp_sol_15m, 12:00 e4 short), a new set key, correctly alerted.
